seasons.listing: SI's Championship Manager 97/98 database as baskeyx extracted it to JSON (github.com/baskeyx/cm9798)
seasons.compiler: baskeyx (Dan Baskey): the cm9798 package, extracted to JSON (commit 06bdd2b, 5 October 2026)
seasons.provenance: The extraction names neither the tool that read the game's files nor the game's version (2.81 or 2.93), and it holds Scandinavian, Japanese, Turkish and MLS divisions the UK release did not play, so it may come from another release or an edited database. No second copy of its values exists. Its transfers stop in September 1997: Ravanelli is at Marseille and Yeboah at Hamburg, Karembeu still at Sampdoria, Klinsmann at Sampdoria and Davids at Milan. For the same players its abilities run about 9 points above the next season's on the 1-200 scale (110.9 against 101.4 in the CM3 port for 7,435 players matched by name and nation, correlation 0.69, 27% identical; 9.5 above SI's 3.9.60), so its ratings sit about 4.7 higher across the board; the conversion is CM 01/02's, unchanged.
seasons.rights: The package's code is MIT; its player and team data, extracted from the game, is not, and its rights stay with Sports Interactive and Eidos.

seasons.provenance: Row for row the spreadsheet; its Swedish club records equal the game's own team file (304 of 304 players), and its national squads gazchap's database (64 of 64 checked). A SWOS United thread (2021) says some minor nations' squads and nationalities in the game predate 1996.
seasons.rights: Sensible World of Soccer is Sensible Software's, published by Renegade and GT Interactive and now Codemasters'; the database's code is MIT, the game's data is not.
